verdict.rationale: Svelte's own sources say it is a compiler that turns declarative components into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM, so the browser does minimal work. Community users corroborate the compile-to-imperative-JS model and readable compiled output. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that no virtual DOM diffing step exists, and independent benchmarks of DOM-update performance (one user reports rendering limits at high element counts).

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on a compiler-optimized rendering system that updates the DOM without a virtual DOM diffing step

citations.quote: It's a compiler that takes your declarative components and converts them into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM.
a UI framework that uses a compiler to let you write breathtakingly concise components that do minimal work in the browser
It uses a compiler to turn declarative components written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript...into lean, tightly optimized JavaScript.
The generated code is readable: they stepped through compiled component code while profiling a layout-per-frame issue and traced it to their own function.
